why: When service=='catalog' and method is 'createImage' or 'updateImage', server.ts's make_api_request handler (server.ts:189-224) forwards params.request verbatim as `args` into CatalogHandlers.createImage/updateImage (services/catalog.ts:436-512 and 514-607). Those handlers read the caller-supplied 'image_file' string (marked isFile:true in utils/type-map.ts:4427-4432 and 6628-6633, with description 'Path to the image file to upload', which is exactly what get_type_info would hand back to the caller) directly off `args[field]` with zero sanitization: fs.existsSync only checks existence (not location), there is no path.resolve+prefix check, no realpath confinement to an allowed directory, and no rejection of absolute paths or '../' traversal. Because the caller already fully controls the same make_api_request tool, they can immediately follow up with catalog.getObject/catalog.list (also via make_api_request) to retrieve the resulting image's public URL and download the exfiltrated file content back out -- a complete confidentiality-impacting arbitrary local file read/exfiltration path, not mere robustness or a crash.
